faqs.q: What is Grade 100 Alloy Lifting Chain used for?
faqs.a: Grade 100 Alloy Lifting Chain is Grade 100 alloy steel chain used to make chain slings and as load chain in hoists, rated by working load limit. It is listed in 14 sizes, 6 mm to 26 mm.

faqs.q: How do I read an Indus part number for Grade 100 Alloy Lifting Chain, such as IH-LR-CH-G100-6MM?
faqs.a: Grade 100 Alloy Lifting Chain part numbers begin with IH-LR-CH-G100 and end in a size code: IH-LR-CH-G100-6MM is the 6 mm size and IH-LR-CH-G100-26MM is the 26 mm size. Quote the full part number from the size table, or give us the size and the load you need, when you enquire.

faqs.q: What sizes does Grade 100 Alloy Lifting Chain come in?
faqs.a: Grade 100 Alloy Lifting Chain is listed in 14 sizes, 6 mm to 26 mm, each with its own Indus part number, for example IH-LR-CH-G100-6MM and IH-LR-CH-G100-26MM. The table includes 6 mm: WLL 1.4 t, minimum breaking load 57 kN, proof load 35 kN and 26 mm: WLL 26.5 t, minimum breaking load 1062 kN, proof load 664 kN.

faqs.q: How do I choose the right size of Grade 100 Alloy Lifting Chain?
faqs.a: For Grade 100 Alloy Lifting Chain, choose the chain size from the working load limit you need for the sling or hoist configuration, and pair it with hooks, links and shackles of the same grade and size. Proof and breaking forces are test figures, not working limits; sizes outside the standard rating table have their WLL confirmed on the quotation.

faqs.q: What is the rated load of Grade 100 Alloy Lifting Chain?
faqs.a: Grade 100 Alloy Lifting Chain is listed with a working load limit 1.4 to 26.5 t; minimum breaking load 57 to 1,062 kN. For example, 18 mm: WLL 12.5 t, minimum breaking load 509 kN, proof load 318 kN. The working load is the figure to lift or load to; proof and breaking loads are test figures and never working limits.

faqs.q: What is Grade 100 Alloy Lifting Chain made from, and what finish does it have?
faqs.a: For Grade 100 Alloy Lifting Chain, the material is Alloy steel. If your site needs a particular material grade, coating or material certificate, say so on the enquiry and we confirm it before the order.

faqs.q: What standard and certificate apply to Grade 100 Alloy Lifting Chain?
faqs.a: Grade 100 Alloy Lifting Chain is listed to Grade 100. The listing gives its documentation as: Manufacturer's test certificate. For third-party certification or a witnessed proof test, say so on the RFQ before the order is placed.

faqs.q: What does Grade 100 Alloy Lifting Chain connect to or work with?
faqs.a: For Grade 100 Alloy Lifting Chain, hooks, master links and connecting links must be of the same grade and size as the chain. Matching Grade 100 parts are on our [Grade 100 chain fittings shelf](/c/grade-100-chain-fittings), and the chain is made up into slings on the [chain slings shelf](/c/chain-slings).

faqs.q: How should Grade 100 Alloy Lifting Chain be inspected and looked after?
faqs.a: For Grade 100 Alloy Lifting Chain, check the chain along its whole length for stretched links, nicks, gouges, bent or twisted links and wear where links bear on each other, and remove any damaged length from service. Lifting chain also needs periodic inspection by a competent person.

faqs.q: How does Grade 100 Alloy Lifting Chain differ from Grade 80 Alloy Lifting Chain?
faqs.a: Grade 100 Alloy Lifting Chain differs from [Grade 80 Alloy Lifting Chain](/p/grade-80-alloy-lifting-chain) in its pattern / standard Grade 100 against Grade 80; size range 6 mm to 26 mm against 6 mm (1/4″) to 26 mm (1″). It also differs in its working load limit 1.4 to 26.5 t against 1,150 to 20,000 kg.

Give us the part numbers, quantities and delivery country through our contact page and we quote the freight and lead time with the price.
